discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulating states and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: strongly correlated quantum materials
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees, the Dirac velocity of bilayer graphene vanishes and nearly flat moire bands emerge, so that electron interactions dominate kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group realized this experimentally, discovering correlated Mott-like insulating states and unconventional superconductivity that can be tuned by a gate voltage in a single device. This work created the field of twistronics and moire quantum matter. It gives us a clean, tunable platform where the Hubbard-type physics of the cuprates and transition-metal oxides can be explored by turning a knob, rather than through chemistry. It has since produced orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect and fractional Chern insulators in moire systems. A sharp theoretical prediction followed by a decisive experiment has transformed the study of strongly correlated electrons.
